title: Psst! Toy Story 5 Has Secret Scenes After the Credits!
summary: Have you ever sat through a whole movie, then the lights come on and your parents say "let's go" — but you have a feeling there's MORE? Well, for Toy Story 5, you'll want to glue yourself to that seat! This new adventure brings Woody, Buzz, Jessie, and the gang face-to-face with a shiny tablet named Lilypad (voiced by Greta Lee). She thinks she knows what's best for their kid, Bonnie. But here's the real secret: after the story ends and the credits start rolling, don't move! There's a mid-credits scene — that means a short extra clip while names are still on screen. And if you wait even longer, until every single name has scrolled by, there's another tiny surprise at the very end. It's like a hidden bonus level in a video game! The scenes aren't super important to the main story, but they're fun treats for fans. Director Andrew Stanton (who made WALL-E and Finding Dory) tucked them in there. So when you go see Toy Story 5, remember: the movie isn't really over until the screen goes completely dark. Stay put, munch your popcorn slowly, and enjoy every last second!
why_it_matters: It reminds you that sometimes the best surprises come to those who wait patiently, even when everyone else is ready to leave.

background_read: After a movie ends, the credits roll to thank everyone who worked on it. Some directors hide short extra scenes in the credits to give fans a fun surprise.
This tradition has become popular in many animated and superhero movies, making the final moments even more exciting.
Toy Story is a series of movies made by Pixar Animation Studios, which often adds hidden details and jokes for careful viewers.
Article_Structure: WHO: Woody, Buzz, Jessie, Bonnie, Lilypad (voice by Greta Lee), and director Andrew Stanton.
WHAT: Toy Story 5 has two hidden scenes during and after the credits that are fun treats for fans.
WHERE: In the movie theater, after the main story ends and the lights come on.
WHY: The director tucked them in as a reward for fans who stay until the very end of the movie.

perspectives.description: Staying to watch every second shows you care about the movie, and the hidden scenes feel like a special gift.
Sitting through all the credits can feel boring, especially if your parents are in a hurry to go home.
The extra scenes are not important to the main story, so it's okay to skip them if you are not a big fan.
